public_rationale: Supported on the retrospective, ordinary reading. The survey documents increasing actual AI use in development. A developer study records a participant proceeding without understanding generated code. Another documents generated insecure SQL code being copied into a solution. These support the modest claim that such problems had occurred in some cases. The C study found little added security risk in its setting, so the evidence does not justify a broader claim that AI assistance generally makes code less secure.
limitations: The context creates a material timing ambiguity between the recalled early-2025 warning and an October 2026 observation.
Adoption evidence is broader than code generation alone and reflects survey respondents.
Controlled studies demonstrate possibilities and examples, not industry-wide harm rates.

At the beginning of 2025 I warned
our_interpretation: The passage recalls an early-2025 warning. I assess the adoption trend and documented examples available by that warning, using January 2025 as the approximate endpoint. No starting date is specified.
The ordinary reading is growing adoption of generative coding tools, documented instances of incomplete understanding, and demonstrated vulnerabilities introduced through generated code.
Laboratory demonstrations qualify as cases already shown. The wording does not require a production breach, a previously unknown vulnerability class, or worse security on average.
The latest completed annual survey before the recalled warning can measure the adoption trend. Reported actual use is distinguished from planned use.
criteria.support_condition: Adoption evidence shows increasing use of generative coding tools, and developer studies document both incomplete understanding of generated code and cases where generated code introduces security vulnerabilities.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable adoption evidence establishes declining or unchanged use over the relevant comparison period, or evidence invalidates the claimed examples of incomplete understanding or introduced vulnerabilities. Safe outputs in other cases do not disprove an explicitly limited existence claim.
